page_summary: This page outlines the guidelines for the definition and classification of stages of chronic kidney disease, emphasizing the importance of early detection and treatment.

elements.title: Grading Rationale Statements
clinical_facts: Grade S: Analysis of individual patient data from a single large, generalizable study of high methodological quality (e.g., NHANES III)
Grade C: Compilation of original articles (evidence tables)
Grade R: Review of reviews and selected original articles

elements.title: Definition and Stages of Chronic Kidney Disease
clinical_facts: The presence of chronic kidney disease should be established based on kidney damage and level of kidney function (glomerular filtration rate [GFR]).
Among patients with chronic kidney disease, the stage of disease should be assigned.

page_summary: This page outlines the stages of chronic kidney disease (CKD) according to the K/DOQI classification, detailing the relationship between kidney function and disease severity.

elements.title: Stages of Chronic Kidney Disease
clinical_facts: Stage 1: Kidney damage with normal or increased GFR (≥90 mL/min/1.73 m²)
Stage 2: Kidney damage with mild decreased GFR (60-89 mL/min/1.73 m²)
Stage 3: Moderate decreased GFR (30-59 mL/min/1.73 m²)
Stage 4: Severe decreased GFR (15-29 mL/min/1.73 m²)
Stage 5: Kidney failure (<15 mL/min or dialysis)

page_summary: This page outlines the stages of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and provides guidelines for management and referral based on glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

elements.title: Stages of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Clinical Action Plan
clinical_facts: Stage 1: GFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m² - Diagnosis and treatment, treatment of comorbid conditions, slowing progression.
Stage 2: GFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m² - Estimating progression.
Stage 3: GFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m² - Evaluating and managing complications.
Stage 4: GFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m² - Preparation for kidney replacement therapy.
Stage 5: GFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m² - Replacement (if symptoms present).

relationships.to: kidney damage or GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m² for 3 months

elements.title: Guideline 3: Individuals at Increased Risk of Chronic Kidney Disease
clinical_facts: Individuals without kidney damage and with normal/elevated GFR may be at increased risk for CKD.
Assessment should be part of routine health encounters.
Individuals at risk should undergo testing for markers of kidney damage and GFR estimation.

relationships.to: testing for markers of kidney damage
evaluation and treatment as specified in Guideline 2
